media_work.title: 48 Hours
media_work.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction despite alibis, DNA exoneration after long imprisonment, coerced confession.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction despite alibis, DNA exoneration after long imprisonment, coerced confession.
media_item.summary_notes: Anthony Wright was convicted based on a coerced confession for a 1991 rape/murder in Philadelphia and served nearly 25 years before DNA proved his innocence, leading to acquittal at a 2016 retrial. The case gained further notoriety when detectives involved faced perjury charges related to their testimony at the retrial.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Examines how Wright was convicted of rape/murder despite multiple alibis, later exonerated through DNA after 25 years. Available via CBS/Paramount+.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Rape and Murder (of 77-year-old neighbor Louise Talley)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Anthony Wright was wrongfully convicted of rape and murder in Philadelphia in 1993 and served nearly 25 years. His conviction was based on a coerced false confession, and he was later exonerated in 2016 after DNA evidence proved his innocence. Detectives involved in the case later faced perjury charges.
contributing_factors_raw: Alleged police misconduct (planting evidence, perjury by detectives later charged)
